issue.title: check-web-clip-adapter self-test aborts Chrome under SASE's long TMPDIR (SingletonSocket path too long)

task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
Deterministic, not a flake: `just check-web-clip-adapter` failed identically in bob-cli-52.2's sandbox run and again in bob-cli-52.land's run on master 2d568fa (athena, Chrome at /opt/google/chrome). Both runs failed at Playwright `BrowserType.launch` with `TargetClosedError`. Chrome's own log shows the root cause: `FATAL:chrome/browser/process_singleton_posix.cc:313] Socket path too long: /home/bryan/.cache/sase/tmp/agent-tmp/gh_bobs-org__bob-cli-ws0-261007_081241/bob-clip-test-n55uj49n/com.google.Chrome.pQUZ4v/SingletonSocket`.

Root cause: the adapter's `--self-test` creates its work directories with `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="bob-clip-test-")` (scripts/web_clip/web_clip_adapter.py around lines 2161, 2282 and 2304; also `bob-clip-render-test-` at 2104 and `bob-clip-txt-test-` at 2221) under `$TMPDIR`. Under a SASE agent, `$TMPDIR` is a deep per-agent path. The adapter then sets `TMPDIR=workdir` (line ~1313), so Chrome's SingletonSocket path goes over the 108-byte AF_UNIX limit and Chrome aborts.

Production clips are unaffected. bob's `ScratchDir::create` (src/native/highlights_ref/workdir.rs) already falls back to `/tmp` when `$TMPDIR` is longer than 40 bytes; only the Python self-test skips that guard.

Fix: give the self-test's mkdtemp calls a short base directory, the same way ScratchDir does (use `/tmp` when `$TMPDIR` is longer than 40 bytes). Then confirm `just check-web-clip-adapter` passes when run from a SASE agent workspace.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-52.2 proposed this check-web-clip-adapter failure as a follow-up; the bob-cli-52 landing reproduced it deterministically and found the root cause (an AF_UNIX socket path that is too long), which is unrelated to the epic.
